sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by luminescence complementation on intact (non-permeabilized) cells (L3). Receptor-complex formation on the cell surface in the absence of ligand also confirmed (L4). No downstream signaling (e.g., STAT3 phosphorylation) assay reported in the ledger.
sites.rationale: IL23R has a single-pass type-I topology with one extracellular terminus (the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 24, after cleavage of the 23-aa signal peptide). All ledger clips report N-terminal tags; the only extracellular terminus is therefore the unique landing site, making the junction topology_derived at insert_after_residue=23. Python lookup confirms residue 23 = G (last SP residue) and residue 24 = G (first mature residue); the tag sits 332 residues from the TM boundary, fully satisfying the ≥3-residue clearance rule. L3 provides the most direct surface-display evidence (luminescence on non-permeabilized cells); L4 further shows the tagged receptor retains the ability to form receptor complexes on the cell surface. Full-length human IL23R was expressed with HiBiT or LgBiT fused to its N-terminus in HEK or equivalent mammalian cells (PMC10953408). Addition of exogenous purified complementary NanoBiT fragment to non-permeabilized cells produced luminescence, directly demonstrating that the tag is accessible on the extracellular face. A separate study (PMC10199020, L1) independently constructed HiBiT-IL23R and LgBiT-IL12Rβ1 for cell-surface NanoBiT complementation.

sources.claim: However, when exogenous purified HiBit or LgBit protein was added, luminescence was produced in the presence of the corresponding fragment expressed on the N ‐termini of an IL‐23 receptor monomer.

For the IL23R low Jurkat, the codon-optimized full-length sequence of human IL23R (UniProt # Q5VWK5 ) was tagged N-terminally with a 3x FLAG tag and placed upstream of a furin site, a self-cleavable T2A-peptide, and the sequence of the human IL12Rβ1 subunit.

literature_notes: All six ledger clips (L1–L6) converge on the same physical junction: the N-terminus of mature IL23R immediately after signal-peptide cleavage (after residue 23). No ledger clip reports an internal loop insertion, a C-terminal tag, or any intracellular tag for this protein. L1 and L2 describe construct creation without explicit surface-display data and are therefore subsumed by L3/L4 (NanoBiT surface evidence) and L5/L6 (FLAG surface evidence) respectively. The two sites reported here are the same physical position but grounded in independent papers with different tag chemistries; they are listed separately per the instruction to report every ledger-supported site. No other_positions (intracellular or function-abrogating) appear in the ledger.
